scoring_contract.intermediate_values: Integers between anchors interpolate within the same rubric. Do not imply measured precision beyond evidence.

statuses.numeric: A 0–10 integer is assessed; null means unknown/unassessed. Movie show-only fields are inapplicable and null.
statuses.presence: Use the explicit present/absent/unknown states; never collapse unknown into absence.

scoring_contract.omission: All declared keys are required. Missing keys are contract failures, not zeros or implicit negatives.
scoring_contract.confidence: No calibrated confidence or per-field evidence object is requested. Record assessment_basis honestly; controller-owned source/run records retain actual provenance.
scoring_contract.scope: Every assessment belongs to an explicit movie, whole-show, season, or episode scope with an as-of date and coverage statement.

intensity.10: Exceptionally strong or pervasive in the defined scope.
intensity.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

centrality.0: No narrative importance. The content may be absent or present without a meaningful role; use content_presence separately where covered. Zero alone never certifies absence.
centrality.10: Defining focus; removing it fundamentally changes the work.
centrality.1: Supported, very minor narrative importance; occurrence alone is insufficient. Zero means no narrative importance, not certified absence.

membership.0: Does not use the genre conventions.
membership.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

prominence.8: Prominent across much of the scope.
prominence.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

frequency.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

quality.10: Exceptional execution. Absence is not a zero-quality score.
quality.1: Very unsuccessful execution; not a default for unknown quality or absent craft.

suitability.0: Very poor fit under the stated assumptions.
suitability.10: Exceptionally strong fit. Not a universal audience verdict.

separate_dimensions: Genre membership is not subject presence.
Release era is not setting era.
Production origin is not depicted culture or influence.
Intended audience is not age suitability.
Aesthetic appearance does not establish production technique.
Content presence is not narrative importance: a present detail can have centrality zero. Unknown presence and unknown applicability remain explicit.
scoring_contract.advisory_absence: An absent advisory requires sufficient coverage of the relevant scope and version. Do not turn synopsis silence into absence.
scoring_contract.series_policy: Movie scopes require null for every show-only numeric field and facet. Whole-show assessments name covered seasons; no claims about unassessed later releases.

stakes.cosmic.definition: Consequences extending beyond planetary life to cosmic reality.

stakes.planetary.definition: Consequences extending to a planet or humanity as a whole.

storytelling.educational_intent.definition: Deliberate presentation of factual knowledge for learning.

storytelling.homage.definition: Recognizable tributes and references to other works.

storytelling.narrative_escalation.definition: Strength of progressive intensification in stakes, consequences or conflict across substantial narrative arcs. Distinct from constant high stakes, fast pace, twist count or increasing darkness. A work may escalate without plot twists.

storytelling.narrativity.definition: A developing sequence of causally or temporally linked events organizes the work; 0 indicates non-narrative form, not failure or low quality.

storytelling.pastiche.definition: Imitation or combination of recognizable artistic styles.

storytelling.real_time.definition: Elapsed story time closely tracks presentation time; not simply fast plotting.

storytelling.vignette_structure.definition: Discrete short episodes, scenes or chapters form the work; distinguish from multiple timelines.

tropes.apocalypse_survival.definition: Surviving societal collapse or a world-ending event drives the plot.

tropes.apparent_death.definition: A character appears to die but is later revealed to be alive.

tropes.body_swap.definition: Characters exchange bodies or consciousness across bodies.

tropes.chosen_one.definition: A character is singled out for a special, consequential role.

tropes.conspiracy.definition: Hidden coordination among powerful actors drives the plot.

tropes.doppelganger.definition: A double or lookalike produces meaningful events, identity confusion, recurring humor, or conflict. Antagonism or conflict is not required. Incidental resemblance without a narrative use is insufficient.
tropes.doppelganger.presence_definition: A double or lookalike is presented as such; incidental resemblance alone is insufficient. Conflict is not required.

tropes.final_survivor.definition: A surviving focal character confronts a threat after others are eliminated.

tropes.fish_out_of_water.definition: An unfamiliar social or physical environment challenges a character.

tropes.haunted_house.definition: An inhabited or visited dwelling is the focal site of a haunting.

tropes.hidden_antagonist_reveal.definition: A character's antagonistic role is concealed and later revealed.

tropes.home_invasion.definition: Unwanted hostile entry into a home organizes a consequential part of the story.
tropes.home_invasion.presence_definition: Whether this concept occurs within the assessed scope, independently of narrative importance: Unwanted hostile entry into a home organizes a consequential part of the story.

tropes.locked_room.definition: An apparently inaccessible crime scene creates the central puzzle.

tropes.macguffin_quest.definition: Pursuit of an object whose plot function exceeds its intrinsic characterization.

tropes.memory_loss.definition: Consequential lost or inaccessible memories, missing periods of time, or inability to recall one's own actions. Includes such gaps without a clinical amnesia diagnosis; does not require permanent loss. Ordinary forgetfulness and information withheld only from the audience are insufficient.
tropes.memory_loss.presence_definition: Lost or inaccessible memories or missing periods of a character's own experience occur, whether or not diagnosed as amnesia. Ordinary forgetfulness or withholding information only from the audience is insufficient.

tropes.mentor_death.definition: A mentor dies and the death matters to the mentee's arc.

tropes.mistaken_identity.definition: A character is consequentially taken to be someone else.

tropes.prophecy.definition: Predictions of destiny shape choices and events.

tropes.race_against_time.definition: A consequential deadline structures the conflict.

tropes.rags_to_riches.definition: A character moves from poverty to substantial wealth.

tropes.road_trip.definition: An overland journey with encounters along the way structures the story.

tropes.secret_identity.definition: Concealing an identity or maintaining a double life drives the story.

tropes.single_night.definition: The main action is concentrated in one eventful night.

tropes.tournament.definition: A sequence of competitive rounds structures an arc.

tropes.training.definition: Learning or practice builds abilities toward a later challenge.

tropes.vigilantism.definition: Characters enforce their own justice outside formal authority.

viewing_affordances.background_viewing.definition: Ease of following the work with intermittent attention; not inferred from pace alone.

viewing_affordances.discussion.definition: Scope for discussion of ideas, characters, or interpretation after viewing.

viewing_affordances.drop_in_viewing.definition: Ease of joining after the start without significant confusion.

viewing_affordances.interruption_recover.definition: Ease of regaining the narrative thread after a brief distraction or viewing break without rewinding. Assume a first-time viewer who understood the work up to that point and understands its presentation language. Reorientation cues and intelligible scene goals can help. Distinct from continuous background viewing or joining midway without prior context. Higher means easier recovery, not a greater demand; this is a work-level tendency, not a promise for every interruption or viewer.

viewing_affordances.repeat_discovery.definition: Scope for discovering additional details or interpretations on another viewing; distinct from personal desire to rewatch.

viewing_affordances.standalone_viewing.definition: Ease of understanding this work without other franchise installments.

viewing_affordances.theorizing.definition: Scope for speculation about concealed information or unresolved mysteries.

viewing_demands.attention.definition: Sustained concentration needed to follow the work.

viewing_demands.auditory_dependence.definition: Importance of hearing sound to follow events; accessibility version may alter this.

viewing_demands.cultural_knowledge.definition: Need for cultural background not explained in the work.

viewing_demands.franchise_knowledge.definition: Need for familiarity with other installments to understand this work.

viewing_demands.genre_knowledge.definition: Need for familiarity with genre conventions to understand this work.

viewing_demands.historical_knowledge.definition: Need for historical background not explained in the work.

viewing_demands.inference_load.definition: Demand for working out unstated motives, causal connections or events to follow the work. Distinct from optional deeper interpretation, thematic thought provocation or deliberately unresolved ambiguity. A simple plot may still require substantial inference. Assess an attentive first-time viewer who understands the presentation language.

viewing_demands.information_rate.definition: Rate at which consequential new information arrives and must be processed to follow the work, in speech, images or sound. Distinct from total exposition, dialogue quantity, cutting speed and the pace of physical action. Repetition and rapid movement without new information do not by themselves increase this demand.

viewing_demands.memory_load.definition: Demand for retaining and retrieving names, relationships, clues and earlier details over the assessed work to follow it. Distinct from sustained attention, plot complexity or knowing other installments. Assess an attentive first-time viewer who understands the presentation language; do not assume a particular memory impairment.

viewing_demands.onscreen_reading.definition: Importance of reading text embedded in the image; subtitle demand is derived separately per viewer and offer.

viewing_demands.visual_dependence.definition: Importance of watching the image to understand events; distinct from spectacle.

visuals.aerial_viewpoints.definition: Prominence of aerial views, independently of capture technology.

visuals.aspect_ratio_changes.definition: Expressive use of changes in frame proportions.

visuals.closeups.definition: Prominence of tight framing on faces or details.

visuals.costume_emphasis.definition: Expressive prominence of clothing and costume design.

visuals.digital_effects.definition: Prominence of digitally produced or altered imagery.

visuals.distressed_texture.definition: Deliberate wear, damage, or degraded-image treatment.

visuals.grain_texture.definition: Visible grain-like image texture, independently of capture medium.

visuals.neon_palette.definition: Use of luminous, neon-like color accents.

visuals.practical_effects.definition: Prominence of physical on-set effects; do not infer exact production method from appearance alone.

visuals.restricted_palette.definition: Use of a narrow or monochromatic color range.

visuals.scenic_landscape_prominence.definition: Perceptual emphasis on natural landscapes or scenic built surroundings across the work. Not production location, setting centrality or an automatic judgment of beauty.

visuals.split_screen.definition: Prominence of simultaneous images in separate screen regions.

visuals.static_camera.definition: Locked-off or substantially stationary camera compositions characterize the visual treatment.

presentation.jump_scares.definition: Abrupt audiovisual events deliberately staged to startle. General fear, loudness or sustained tension alone is not a jump scare.

presentation.jump_scare_modalities.definition: Modalities used by actual jump scares, independently of sound-design prominence. Empty only when assessed absent; null when undetermined.

performance.dance_styles.definition: Recognizable dance styles actually depicted in the assessed work, independently of narrative importance. Select all supported styles, including overlaps. Do not infer a style from soundtrack genre, production country, costume alone or combat movement. Broad folk_traditional is not a claim about a particular named tradition; other means a known depicted style outside this bounded vocabulary. Null means the styles cannot be assessed; [] means no listed style identified, not certified absence of all dancing.

performance.dance_contexts.definition: Contexts in which dancing is actually depicted. Select all supported contexts; styles and contexts are whole-work sets and need not describe the same sequence. Narrative musical number includes imagined or expressive dance, not singing alone. Stage performance is different from everyday social dancing; rehearsal is not automatically competition. Null means undetermined; [] means no listed context identified.
